Subject: Compact node-multiplexing & cold-archive backplane plan

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the quick intro call yesterday. I've attached our site inventory (clearwave_site_inventory_0618.csv) but wanted to capture the areas we need Redwood's guidance on before the formal SOW: 

- Cluster footprint: our target is a single 3-rack footprint at the primary site plus an archival appliance in the DR room. We need recommended node counts for small/typical/peak windows.
- Node classes: we want to multiplex CPU-heavy stateless and a small GPU pool for inference bursts. Curious about the tradeoffs if we add an "archive" node class backed by slow block storage for cold model artifacts.
- PV strategy + eviction: guidance on ephemeral PV vs blockstore for cached KV versus long-term archived blobs; eviction thresholds for aggressive reclaim without affecting latency.
- Network & egress: firewall constraints (no outbound except HTTPS through proxy) and limited cross-rack bandwidth during working hours.
- Security: KMS integration required; we will need audit log retention for 18 months.

Can you propose a compact node class matrix and an initial action plan? If useful we can run a 90-minute technical workshop next week (Mon/Tue preferred).

Attaching inventory and a sketch of our current rack layout.

Regards,
Peter Lowe
Head of Infrastructure, ClearSky Health

Peter —

Thanks, received the inventory and sketch. Quick read-through and initial proposals below; attaching a simple node-class matrix (proposed-node-class-matrix.xlsx). Karthik and Neha are looped for details around PVC binding and QoS.

Summary of high-level recommendations (TL;DR):
- Three node classes: control/mgmt (3x m5d-like), compute (mix: 6x c8-like), archive (2x r5d-like with high-capacity HDD or slow NVMe through blockstore gateway).
- Ephemeral PV for runtime caches (small ephemeral local NVMe). Blockstore for model artifacts and long-term retention with lifecycle tiering to the archival appliance.
- Eviction policy: prefer soft-eviction at 70% node disk utilization, hard eviction at 85%. Implement pod disruption budgets and graceful preemption window (30s) for cache pods.
- Networking: recommend a dedicated egress proxy in the mgmt plane to fit constraints; enable cross-rack bandwidth shaping (rate limit during office hours).
- KMS/audit: integrate with customer KMS (we support AWS KMS and external HSM through vault); we can export audit logs to your SIEM for 18 months.

Open questions for the workshop:
1) Is the archival backplane expected to serve models for inference (cold warm transitions) or strictly for storage-only retrieval?
2) Do you have a preferred encryption-at-rest standard (FIPS)?
3) Expected read QPS for archived models (rough ballpark) — affects node counts for archive gateway.

Next steps:
- I'll schedule a 90-minute technical workshop (internal attendees: Karthik, Neha, myself). Please confirm Mon/Tue next week.
- Karthik will prepare PVC binding and QoS recommendations; Neha will draft an eviction/retention policy template we can use in the SOW.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference

Adding a few technical bullets we should cover in the workshop — will convert to a short ops playbook after the call: 

- PVC binding: use ReadWriteOnce block volumes for model artifacts served by a single archive gateway pod; for multi-reader artifacts consider a read-only cached copy on ephemeral NVMe and behind a sidecar cache with LRU.
- QoS classes: set model-serving pods to Guaranteed where latency matters; cache layers can be Burstable with node-level QoS reservations to protect core services.
- Eviction tuning: kubelet eviction thresholds on ephemeral storage: imagefs.available set to 8% and nodefs.available to 7% as a starting point. For preemption, use PodPriority with a mid-tier cache priority; implement a custom eviction hook for graceful checkpointing of in-flight KV flushes.
- Archive gateway: prefer a small stateless gateway (2 replicas) with a background prefetcher that brings frequently used models into the fast cache; this mitigates cold-starts if your read QPS spikes.
- Backups & retention: snapshot model artifacts monthly, keep 3 months on fast blockstore, then move older snapshots to the archival appliance. Verify restore SLA — we should document a 24–72 hour restore window depending on tier.

I'll draft these notes into the shared Drive before the workshop.

— Karthik
